story_theme_en: Chef Ai made 30 chocolate chip cookies and wanted to put them in boxes. Each box must have the same number of cookies, with 6 cookies in each box. Chef Ai needed to know how many boxes she would get. Division helps us share things equally into groups.
helper_tip_en: Have students draw 6 circles and distribute cookies one by one until all are shared equally.
think_story_en: 30 cookies shared into 6 boxes. 30/6 = 5. Each box gets 5 cookies, 5 boxes in total. Check: 5x6=30.

data.question: There are 24 oranges shared equally among 6 friends. How many does each get?

explanation_steps_en: Division as equal sharing means distributing a total amount equally into groups.
In this problem: 30 cookies shared into 6 boxes equally. Each box gets the same number.
30/6 = 5. Each box gets 5 cookies. There are 5 boxes in total.

worked_examples_en.question_en: There are 35 flowers divided into 7 vases equally. How many flowers per vase?

common_mistakes_en: Confusing the dividend (total) with the divisor (number of groups).
Using repeated subtraction instead of division.
Forgetting that division is about equal sharing.
hints_en: Look for clue words: shared equally among, divided into, each.
Use multiplication to check: Quotient x Divisor = Dividend.
Draw circles for each group and distribute items one by one.

explanation_en: Division is sharing equally. Look for shared equally among, divided into, each. Write the total (dividend) first, then the number of groups (divisor). Check by multiplying the quotient by the divisor.
